newsitem.title: CHINA: China Southern to concentrate on passengers.
newsitem.headline: China Southern to concentrate on passengers.

text.p: Concentration by China Southern Airlines Company Limited (CSA) on the Chinese domestic passenger market and its proximity to Hong Kong will limit its focus on air cargo in the short term, Peter Negline, aviation analyst for Salomon Brothers, told Reuters.

Speaking after the publication of Salomon's first report on CSA, in which the investment bank recommended a Hold rating, Negline said CSA's cargo business development will be slower compared to China's two other large airline's, flag carrier Air China and Shanghai-based China Eastern Airlines.

"Cargo will not be a relatively big business at all for CSA in the short term. If it gets serious about its international routes then you will see cargo playing a much bigger role but for the moment CSA is heavily dependent, and concentrating on, the fastest growing domestic market," Negline said in an interview.
CSA's home airport at Guangzhou, 120 kilometres from one of the world's busiest cargo hubs in Hong Kong, was also a major factor affecting CSA's cargo potential, Negline added.

"Hong Kong is so efficient when it comes to cargo handling. that Guangzhou will have to work very hard to catch up. In the long term though, I think we will see a situation like in the London area where Heathrow, like Hong Kong, is dominant but Gatwick, like Gunngzhou, has the potential to play an increasingly important role too," Negline added.

Salomon's said Revenue Tonne Kilometres (RTKs) in freight, which rose from 323 million Renminbi ($39 million) in 1995 to 391 millions in 1996, was estimated to grow to 404 millions in 1998. Total RTKs of both passenger and freight, which totalled 1,428 millions in 1995 and 1,636 millions in 1996, was estimated to grow to 1,841 millions in 1997 and 2,006 millions in 1998.

Freight load factor, which was 35.3 per cent in 1995 and 39.6 per cent in 1996, was estimated to fall to 31.9 per cent in 1997 and 30.9 per cent in 1998, mainly as a result of the airline's increasing capacity.

CSA has rapid expansion plans over the next two years but operating constraints including airport capacity and inadequate air traffic control systems will prevent it and other Chinese carriers from achieving aircraft utilisation rates enjoyed by regional rivals such as Cathay Pacific Airways Limited, the Salomon's report said.
Included in CSA's expansion plans is a dedicated Boeing 737-200 freighter for domestic cargo routes, Salomons added.
